paper.title: Rapamycin fed late in life extends lifespan in genetically heterogeneous mice

organism.source_quote: rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway, extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age

strain.source_quote: Specific pathogen free (SPF) mice were produced at each of the 3 test sites by mating CB6F1 females with C3D2F1 males to produce a genetically heterogeneous population

sex.source_quote: On the basis of age at 90% mortality, rapamycin led to an increase of 14% for females and 9% for males

type.source_quote: rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway

agent.source_quote: rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway

age_at_start.source_quote: extends median and maximal lifespan of both male and female mice when fed beginning at 600 days of age

mechanism.source_quote: rapamycin, an inhibitor of the mTOR pathway

direction.source_quote: mice fed rapamycin were longer lived than controls (p < 0.0001) in both males and females

mean_change_pct.source_quote: Expressed as mean lifespan, the effect sizes were 9% for males and 13% for females in the pooled dataset

max_change_pct.source_quote: On the basis of age at 90% mortality, rapamycin led to an increase of 14% for females and 9% for males

p_value.source_quote: For data pooled across sites, a log-rank test rejected the null hypothesis that treatment and control groups did not differ (p < 0.0001)

experiments.notes: Main cohort only (rapamycin from 600 days). A separate Cohort 2006 (from 270 days) showed reduced mortality at interim analysis but no effect size reported. Total N=1901 across sexes and groups; per-sex N not reported in main text. Dose not stated in main text; microencapsulated rapamycin (Eudragit S100) in 5LG6 chow, blood levels 60-70 ng/ml. Paper speculates anti-neoplastic effects and/or retarded ageing as mechanisms; mTOR inhibition recorded as the stated mechanism of action.
